V-ENCLOSURE.evidence: Dining area under pergola is bounded by the house on one side and open on the other three; fire pit area is open on two sides; pond court is open on two sides.

V-FOCAL.evidence: Large citrus tree in the foreground, fire pit to its left, dining table under pergola to the right, and pond court in the background all compete as focal points.

V-AXIS.evidence: Main gravel path leads to house doors and seating; secondary paths connect dining, fire pit, and BBQ areas; no dead-end paths visible.

V-RHYTHM.evidence: Top right corner shows a distinct mass of four shrubs planted in a tight group. Bottom left shows a large mass of ground cover/perennials under a small tree. These represent clear repeated groups rather than scattered singles.

V-LAYERING.evidence: Top right corner shows a cluster of light green circles (shrubs) overlapping a blue area (pond), with a row of small circles (ground cover) behind them. Bottom left shows a large dark green circle (canopy tree) over a medium green circle (small tree).

V-ROOMS.evidence: Distinct zones include a gravel fire pit area, a paved dining area under a pergola, a paved standing/BBO area, and a separate herbs bed, each with different floor surfaces and uses.

V-OVERALL.evidence: Clear zoning into distinct rooms (dining, fire pit, herbs, pond court), defined edges via walls and paving, and structured planting masses (citrus, shrubs, ground cover) create a cohesive, designed landscape.
